from: August book, night 16 (Friends Who Sat Close)
p1: Then Job got very sick, with sore spots from his feet to his head. He sat in the ashes, sad and hurting.
Three friends heard about Job’s troubles: Eliphaz, Bildad and Zophar. They came to comfort Job and help him feel better.
When they saw Job, they cried out loud. They tossed dust on their heads, the way people then showed sadness.
p2: Then they sat with Job on the ground for seven days and seven nights. No one said a word, because they saw how sad he was. After that, Job told them how very sad he felt.
When someone you love is sad, you can sit close. Tonight, think of one person you can sit by tomorrow.
old: When Job was sad and not feeling well, his friends heard about it. They wanted to help, so they came to be with him.
At first, Job’s friends didn’t say a single word. They just sat quietly beside him for a long, long time.
Sometimes when someone is sad, the kindest thing is simply to be near them. Job’s friends showed love just by staying close.
Being there for a sad friend is a beautiful gift. A quiet hug or a hand to hold can say, “I love you, and you’re not alone.” Heavenly Father loves it when we comfort one another.
